title: Holding Several Northgate Care Protection Plans
content:
A member may hold any number of Northgate Care Protection Plans contracts, one for each covered product. There is no cap on the number of plans one member may hold.

Every plan stands alone. Its limit of liability, its claim counts, its refunds and its term are never pooled with those of another plan, even where the covered products were bought on the same purchase.

## What standing alone means for each plan

| Element | Belongs to |
|---|---|
| Limit of liability | that plan only — the price of the product it covers |
| Claim counts (repairs of a failure, accidental damage claims) | that plan only |
| Refunds | that plan only — each plan's own charge |
| Term (coverage start and end dates) | that plan only |

## Hypothetical illustrations

- A member who bought a television and a laptop on one receipt, each covered by its own Northgate Care plan, holds two plans. A repair paid on the television plan does not reduce the laptop plan's limit of liability, and the two plans' terms are counted separately.
- A member holding four Northgate Care plans — one on a refrigerator, one on a washer, one on a mattress and one on a television — may buy a fifth for another covered product; the number already held is no bar.
- Two accidental damage claims settled on one Northgate Care 3-Year Electronics Plan with Accident Protection do not count against a second such plan the same member holds on another product.
